newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand grants displaced Burmese citizenship.
newsitem.headline: Thailand grants displaced Burmese citizenship.

text.p: Nearly 8,000 Burmese living illegally in Thailand for more than 20 years will be given Thai citizenship, government officials said on Tuesday.
Thailand's cabinet approved on Tuesday an interior ministry proposal to grant citizenship to 7,849 displaced Burmese living in the country.
"These people are Thais who happened to live in Burma because of the common border. They have a right to gain Thai citizenship," said Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh after a cabinet meeting.
Thailand is faced with a major illegal immigrant problem. Nearly a million Asian economic migrants, particularly Burmese and Cambodians, work in the country as poorly paid labourers.
In addition, some 100,000 ethnic Karen refugees, who have fled from fighting in eastern Burma, have been living in refugee camps in western Thailand for more than a decade.
